title: Import-to-GMA review step: don't style clickable actions as static badges
answers: Why does the Preview control on the Import wizard review step look like a badge instead of a button?
How should I add an interactive action next to a static status label in the Review step cards?
Preview icon/badge is not perceivable as clickable
body:
Symptom: Users reported the 'Preview' control on the Review step (Notification Resources / Alert Rules cards) looked identical to the static, non-interactive 'Skipped' badge next to it — nothing signaled it was clickable except a tiny eye icon.
Root cause: the control was a plain <button> styled with a custom CSS class (`styles.badgeWithIcon` in public/app/features/alerting/unified/components/import-to-gma/ImportToGMA.tsx) that visually matched the success-colored status badges on the same screen.
Fix pattern: split status text from the action — render the status as plain `Text` and render the action as a real `Button` (variant="secondary", icon="eye") from `@grafana/ui`, so interactive controls are visually and semantically distinct from static badges/labels.
Constraints: applies to any review/summary screen mixing static status indicators with clickable affordances; don't reuse badge-style CSS classes for anything with an onClick handler.
applies: Alerting Import-to-GMA wizard Review step; generally any UI mixing static status badges with clickable preview/action controls
